newsitem.title: GERMANY: German FDP defends tax reform, agrees early date.
newsitem.headline: German FDP defends tax reform, agrees early date.

text.p: The leader of Germany's centrist Free Democrats on Friday defended the government's tax reform proposals, arguing the massive cuts in the income tax rates would give the economy a spurt and create jobs.

Wolfgang Gerhardt, chairman of the FDP, said during a debate in parliament that the FDP was also willing to work out a plan to move forward the date of the proposed tax reform by one year to January 1998.
"There will be an enormous increase in jobs," Gerhardt said. "The primary goal of the tax cuts is raising the chances for new jobs."
